headlines.title: Trump calls Nvidia CEO to talk AI — and gets put on speakerphone during industry summit
headlines.description: “Data centers are great, and they make people wealthy,” the president told CEO Jensen Huang, whose company makes AI chips and hardware.

headlines.title: Trump says AI doesn’t need guardrails, calls growing concerns ‘a hoax’
headlines.description: The president also alleged the existence of a “sick conspiracy” against AI and data centers, at a time when Americans are increasingly concerned about the technology.

headlines.title: U.S. and China face grave AI risks but mutual distrust stalls cooperation
headlines.description: The United States and China are both gripped by safety fears as they reckon with their rapid advances in AI, but intensifying competition and deep mutual distrust could derail the kind of cooperation experts say is vital to head off the strategically vital technology’s greatest dangers.

headlines.title: Trump calls concerns over A.I. destroying humanity a 'hoax'
headlines.description: President Trump waded deep into the current debate over the safety of artificial intelligence as leaders throughout the tech industry are warning of its risks and urging a slow down in development. NBC News’ Chief Business Correspondent Christine Romans reports.

headlines.title: Supreme Court Blocks Trump’s Bid to Restrict Mail-in Ballot Rules
headlines.description: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected President Donald Trump’s efforts to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterm elections in November. NBC’s Laura Jarrett joins TODAY to break down what’s at stake with the decision.

headlines.title: Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board again votes to close venue, calling it ‘unsafe’
headlines.description: President Donald Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board voted Tuesday to immediately shutter the performing arts center, a source familiar with the decision said, after its members argued the institution is in “dire” financial and structural shape.

headlines.title: Trump Dismisses Dangers of AI: ‘The Whole Thing is a Hoax’
headlines.description: While most lawmakers are saying it’s time to enact guardrails against AI, President Donald Trump is continuing to downplay the potential dangers. In a surprise on-stage call to the head of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, the president said, “The robots will not be taking over…The whole thing is a hoax.” Instead, he’s framing the AI arms race as one to win. NBC’s Hallie Jackson reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Director Alex Gibney explores Elon Musk’s power in new documentary
headlines.description: “Musk”, the new four-hour documentary from director Alex Gibney, has been gaining buzz after appearances at film festivals in Venice and Toronto and chronicles the life of Elon Musk through his early days in Silicon Valley to his actions in politics. NPR technology correspondent Bobby Allyn saw the film and talks with NBC News’ Gadi Schwartz about its message.

headlines.title: Top AI Developers Warn the Technology is Developing Too Rapidly
headlines.description: Some of the world’s leading creators of AI are uniting in warning of the dangers of the technology advancing too quickly and publicly calling for a slowdown. They say that it could, in the not-too-distant future, actually outsmart the researchers who are building it and pose an existential threat to humanity. NBC’s Christine Romans reports and Josh Tyrangiel, staff writer at The Atlantic and author of "AI for Good: How Real People Are Using Artificial Intelligence to Fix Things That Matter,"

headlines.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
headlines.description: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.

headlines.title: Anthropic Says it Blocked Efforts to Use AI for Biological Weapons
headlines.description: AI company Anthropic says it uncovered multiple attempts by researchers linked to foreign governments to use Claude and other tools for work that could lead to deadly bioweapons. That research was detected and blocked by Anthropic but experts say this kind of example is just the tip of the iceberg. NBC’s Christine Romans reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: More AI researchers warn of AI's threat to humanity
headlines.description: NBC News' Tom Llamas spoke to two more artificial intelligence researchers about the potential threat A.I has to humanity. This comes after AI researcher Jacob Coxon shared a viral tweet saying he believed AI could kill humanity in the next decade. Llamas also spoke to Incoming Professor at UC Berkley Sayash Kapoor who also warns of risk, but says policy proposals and regulations can help prevent further threats.
